title: Unified structured-log collector & canonicalizer for multi-tenant pipelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Replace several service-specific log shims with a single front-line structured-log collector that normalizes JSON/JSONL inputs, canonicalizes correlation identifiers, emits tenant-aware labels, and routes to Loki and Elasticsearch backends. The goal is to reduce downstream parsing variance, make trace <-> log joins reliable, and provide deterministic labels for latency/error dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: All incoming JSON/JSONL log streams are validated against a lightweight schema and malformed events are routed to a quarantine topic with reason metadata.

A canonical correlation_id field is populated for 99.9% of application events via: incoming trace/span propagation, header extraction, or stable session hashing, with a marked confidence tag when synthesized.

Loki push payloads include a normalized set of labels: tenant_id, service, env, shard, correlation_id and a minimal free-text message field; label cardinality is capped via configurable bucketing rules.
Elasticsearch index mapping contains dedicated fields for trace_id, span_id, correlation_id, and structured attributes; mappings are backward-compatible with current dashboards.

End-to-end latency from ingress proxy to Loki/ES index does not exceed current SLO (95th percentile under typical load) and backpressure paths are functional under overload (messages persist to compacted Kafka topic and an alert is raised).
Unit and integration tests for schema negotiation, correlation propagation, and tenant label derivation are present and reviewed.
technical_notes: Ingress architecture: replace 3 language-specific sidecars with a single Go-based collector that performs streaming JSON decoding, schema-first field normalization, pluggable enrichment hooks, and synchronous/async routing decisions.

Correlation logic: prefer otel.trace_id and x-request-id headers; fallback to deterministic tenant-scoped session fingerprinting (sha1(service+session_cookie+low_entropy_id)) and attach correlation_confidence:high|medium|low.

Sampling & dedup: use probabilistic sampling flags for high-volume tenants at ingress and strip duplicate events detected by (tenant, event_id, timestamp window). Dedup heuristics configurable per-tenant.

Label cardinality control: implement bucketing for user_id/account_id labels and a policy engine to drop or hash high-card fields when label_count>threshold; expose per-tenant label budgets in Console.

Routing: primary sink is Loki via push API for line/stream queries; ES is an optional enrichment sink for long-term analytics. Use compacted Kafka topic as write-ahead for both sinks to enable replay and retry without data loss.

Schema evolution: support versioned lightweight schemas (jsonschema v7) with transformation rules to upgrade older events on ingest. Quarantined events should include original payload and failure_reason in S3 for audit.

Backpressure & SLOs: when downstream is slow, throttle per-tenant ingestion and mark traces/logs with ingestion_delay_ms, increment per-tenant overload metric, and trigger pager if queued_highwater > configured threshold.
Security & PII: implement optional field redaction rules driven by tenant policy (regex or path-based); integrate with KMS for audit of redaction rules changes.
timeline: MVP (schema normalization + correlation canonicalization + Loki routing) in 3 sprints; subsequent sprints for ES enrichment, policy-driven bucketing, and Console controls.
